facts.statement: Gallimimus is a genus of dinosaur.
facts.quote: genus: Gallimimus

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gallimimus is Gallimimus bullatus.
facts.quote: species: bullatus

facts.statement: Gallimimus was described by Osmólska and colleagues in 1972.
facts.quote: authority: Osmólska et al., 1972

facts.statement: Ornithomimus bullatus is a synonym of Gallimimus bullatus.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Ornithomimus bullatus Paul, 1988

facts.statement: Fossils of Gallimimus were discovered by Polish-Mongolian expeditions in the Gobi Desert during the 1960s.
facts.quote: Several fossils in various stages of growth were discovered by Polish-Mongolian expeditions in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the 1960s

facts.statement: A large skeleton found in the region became the holotype for Gallimimus bullatus in 1972.
facts.quote: a large skeleton discovered in this region was made the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Gallimimus bullatus in 1972.

facts.statement: Gallimimus is the largest known member of the ornithomimid group.
facts.quote: Gallimimus is the largest known ornithomimid

facts.statement: Adult Gallimimus measured about 6 meters in length, 1.9 meters in height at the hip, and weighed between 400 and 490 kilograms.
facts.quote: adults were about 6 m long, 1.9 m tall at the hip and weighed about 400 - 490 kg.

facts.statement: It is highly likely that Gallimimus had feathers, based on evidence from its relative Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: As evidenced by its relative Ornithomimus, it is highly likely it would have had feathers.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had a small, light head with large eyes facing to the sides.
facts.quote: The head was small and light with large eyes that faced to the sides.

facts.statement: Gallimimus was toothless, possessed a keratinous beak, and had a delicate lower jaw.
facts.quote: Gallimimus was toothless with a keratinous (horny) beak, and had a delicate lower jaw.

facts.statement: Many vertebrae of Gallimimus had openings indicating they were pneumatic or air-filled.
facts.quote: Many of the vertebrae had openings that indicate they were pneumatic (air-filled).

facts.statement: Gallimimus had a neck that was proportionally long relative to its trunk.
facts.quote: The neck was proportionally long in relation to the trunk.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had hands that were proportionally the shortest among ornithomimosaurs, with three digits each bearing curved claws.
facts.quote: The hands were proportionally the shortest of any ornithomimosaur and each had three digits with curved claws.

facts.statement: Gallimimus was a fast-running animal that used its speed to escape predators.
facts.quote: As an ornithomimid, Gallimimus would have been a fleet (or cursorial) animal, using its speed to escape predators

facts.statement: The estimated running speed of Gallimimus was between 42 and 56 kilometers per hour.
facts.quote: its speed has been estimated at 42–56 km/h (29–34 mph).

facts.statement: Gallimimus may have lived in groups, a hypothesis based on the discovery of multiple specimens in a bone bed.
facts.quote: Gallimimus may have lived in groups, based on the discovery of several specimens preserved in a bone bed.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Gallimimus used beak structures for filter-feeding in water or for feeding on tough plant material as a herbivore.
facts.quote: It has also been suggested that it used small columnar structures in its beak for filter-feeding in water, though these structures may instead have been ridges used for feeding on tough plant material, indicative of a herbivorous diet.

facts.statement: Polish-Mongolian paleontological expeditions to the Gobi Desert were organized between 1963 and 1965.
facts.quote: Between 1963 and 1965, the Polish Academy of Sciences and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences organised the Polish-Mongolian palaeontological expeditions to the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The largest skeleton, which later became the holotype of Gallimimus bullatus, was discovered by Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska in 1964.
facts.quote: The largest skeleton (later to become the holotype of Gallimimus bullatus) was discovered by palaeontologist Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska in Tsaagan Khushuu in 1964

facts.statement: Gallimimus bullatus was named in 1972 by Halszka Osmólska, Ewa Roniewicz, and Rinchen Barsbold.
facts.quote: In 1972, palaeontologists Halszka Osmólska, Ewa Roniewicz and Rinchen Barsbold named the new genus and species Gallimimus bullatus

facts.statement: At the time of description, twenty-five specimens of Gallimimus were known, nine of which consisted of single bones.
facts.quote: Osmólska and colleagues listed twenty-five known specimens in all, nine of which were only represented by single bones.

facts.statement: A slab containing two Gallimimus specimens was repatriated to Mongolia in 2014 after being smuggled to the US.
facts.quote: In 2014, a slab with two Gallimimus specimens was repatriated to Mongolia along with other dinosaur skeletons, after having been smuggled to the US.

facts.statement: In 2017, a fossil trackway associated with a Gallimimus foot was reported, having been discovered in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2017, Hang-Jae Lee and colleagues reported a fossil trackway discovered in 2009 associated with a clenched Gallimimus foot (specimen MPC-D100F/17).

facts.statement: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul moved most ornithomimid species into the genus Ornithomimus, creating the combination O. bullatus.
facts.quote: In 1988, the palaeontologist Gregory S. Paul concluded that the skulls of ornithomimids were more similar to each other than previously thought and moved most species into the same genus, Ornithomimus, resulting in the new combination O. bullatus.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul later listed the species as Gallimimus (or Struthiomimus) bullatus in 2010 before reverting to Gallimimus in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2010, he instead listed it as "Gallimimus (or Struthiomimus) bullatus", but returned to using only the genus name Gallimimus in 2016.

facts.statement: Most other paleontologists have kept the species involved in separate genera rather than grouping them under Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: The species involved have generally been kept in separate genera by other writers.

facts.statement: Barsbold noted morphological variation among newer Gallimimus specimens, but this observation has never been published.
facts.quote: Barsbold noted some morphological variation among newer Gallimimus specimens, though this has never been published.

facts.statement: In 2006, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Barsbold proposed that a nearly complete skeleton informally named Gallimimus mongoliensis probably belongs to a different genus.
facts.quote: Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Barsbold proposed in 2006 that it probably belongs to a different genus.

facts.statement: The adult holotype of Gallimimus was about 6 meters long, 1.9 meters tall at the hip, with a 330 mm skull and a 660 mm femur.
facts.quote: The adult holotype (specimen IGM 100/11) was about 6 m long and 1.9 m tall at the hip; its skull was 330 mm long and the femur (thigh bone) was 660 mm.

facts.statement: The adult Gallimimus would have weighed between 400 and 490 kg.
facts.quote: It would have weighed about 400 - 490 kg.

facts.statement: A juvenile Gallimimus specimen was about 2.15 meters long, 0.79 meters tall at the hip, and weighed between 26 and 30.2 kg.
facts.quote: In comparison, one juvenile specimen (ZPAL MgD-I/94) was about 2.15 m long, 0.79 m tall at the hip, and weighed about 26 - 30.2 kg.

facts.statement: Evidence from related Ornithomimus suggests Gallimimus was feathered and had wing-like structures indicated by quill-knobs on the ulna bone.
facts.quote: Based on fossils of the related Ornithomimus, it is known that ornithomimosaurs ("ostrich dinosaurs") were feathered, and that the adults bore wing-like structures as evidenced by the presence of quill-knobs on the ulna bone of the lower arm, bumps that indicate where feathers would have attached.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had a long skull with a gently convex sloping upper profile on its snout, longer than in other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Due to the length of its snout, the skull was long compared to other ornithomimids, and the snout had a gently convex sloping upper profile.

facts.statement: Viewed from above, the Gallimimus snout was spoon-shaped and U-shaped at the tip, unlike the V-shaped snouts of North American ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Seen from above, the snout was almost spatulate (spoon-shaped), broad and rounded at the tip (or U-shaped), whereas it was acute (or V-shaped) in North American ornithomimids.

facts.statement: The orbits of Gallimimus were large and faced sideways, similar to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The orbits (eye sockets) were large and faced sideways, as in other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: The front of the Gallimimus mandible was shovel-like, creating a gap between the jaw tips when shut.
facts.quote: The front of the mandible was shovel-like, resulting in a gap between the tips of the jaws when shut.

facts.statement: The shovel-like shape of the Gallimimus beak was similar to that of a common seagull.
facts.quote: The shovel-like shape was similar to that of the common seagull, and the lower beak may have had a shape similar to that of this bird.

facts.statement: The jaws of Gallimimus were toothless and covered in a keratinous rhamphotheca (horny beak) at the front.
facts.quote: The jaws of Gallimimus were edentulous (toothless), and the front part would have been covered in a keratinous rhamphotheca (horny beak) in life.

facts.statement: The inner side of the Gallimimus beak had small, tightly packed columnar structures that were longest at the front and shortened towards the back.
facts.quote: The inner side of the beak had small, tightly packed and evenly spaced columnar structures (their exact nature is debated), which were longest at the front and shortening towards the back.

facts.statement: Gallimimus possessed 64 to 66 vertebrae in its spine, which is fewer than in other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Gallimimus had 64–66 vertebrae in its spine, fewer than other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had a neck that was proportionally longer relative to its trunk compared to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The neck appears to have been proportionally longer in relation to the trunk than in other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had three similarly developed fingers, where the first was the strongest, the third the weakest, and the second the longest.
facts.quote: It had three fingers, which were similarly developed; the first (the "thumb") was the strongest, the third was the weakest and the second was the longest.

facts.statement: Gallimimus lacked a hallux, or dewclaw, which is the first toe found in most other theropods.
facts.quote: The foot had no hallux (or dewclaw, the first toe of most other theropods).

facts.statement: Gallimimus possessed an arctometatarsalian foot structure where the lower half of the third metatarsal narrowed and wedged between the second and fourth metatarsals.
facts.quote: The lower half of the third metatarsal was broad when viewed end on, partly covering the adjoining two metatarsals to each side, but narrowed abruptly at mid-length, wedging between those bones and disappearing (an arctometatarsalian foot structure).

facts.statement: Barsbold established the new group Ornithomimosauria in 1976 to include the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: In 1976, Barsbold placed Ornithomimidae in the new group Ornithomimosauria.

facts.statement: Gallimimus belonged to the clade Maniraptoriformes within coelurosaurian theropods, a group that also includes modern birds.
facts.quote: Ornithomimosaurs belonged to the clade Maniraptoriformes of coelurosaurian theropods, which also includes modern birds.

facts.statement: Gallimimus and related ornithomimosaurs lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: The group must have dispersed once or twice from Asia to North America across Beringia to account for the Late Cretaceous genera found there.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the classification of Asian ornithomimids into the same families as North American relatives is appropriate, as these categories were more inclusive than those used for modern birds.
facts.quote: In 1975, Kielan-Jaworowska stated that though many dinosaurs from Asia were placed in the same families as North American relatives, this category of classification tended to be more inclusive than was used for modern birds.

facts.statement: Osmólska and colleagues found that the hands of Gallimimus were not prehensile and the thumb was not opposable.
facts.quote: Osmólska and colleagues found that the hands of Gallimimus were not prehensile (or capable of grasping), and that the thumb was not opposable.

facts.statement: Dale Russell suggested in 1972 that ornithomimids like Gallimimus were very fleet or cursorial animals.
facts.quote: They agreed with the interpretations of ornithomimid biology by palaeontologist Dale Russell from earlier in 1972, including that they would have been very fleet (or cursorial) animals

facts.statement: Paul suggested that the relatively short tails and missing halluxes of ornithomimids were adaptations for speed.
facts.quote: Paul considered the relatively short tails, which reduced weight, and missing halluxes of ornithomimids to be adaptations for speed.

facts.statement: The simultaneous death of Gallimimus individuals may indicate that the species was gregarious or lived in groups.
facts.quote: The fact that the animals seem to have died at the same time (the empty excavation pits were stratigraphically identical) may indicate that Gallimimus was gregarious (lived in groups), which has also been suggested for other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: The genus Gallimimus was described by Osmólska, Roniewics & Barsbold in 1972.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osmólska, Roniewics & Barsbold, 1972

facts.quote: species_authority: Osmólska, Roniewics & Barsbold, 1972

facts.quote: synonyms: * "Sanchusaurus" Hisa, 1988

facts.statement: Gallimimus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Gallimimus fossils were found in the Nemegt Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Fue hallado en la Formación Nemegt, en Mongolia.

facts.statement: Gallimimus resembled an ostrich due to its long neck and toothless beak.
facts.quote: Su aspecto recuerda al de un avestruz dado su largo cuello y su pico sin dientes.

facts.statement: The adult holotype of Gallimimus would have weighed approximately 440 kilograms.

facts.statement: Based on relative fossils, ornithomimids like Gallimimus had feathers and adults carried wing-like structures indicated by knobs on the ulna.
facts.quote: Sobre la base de los fósiles de los parientes Ornithomimus, se sabe que los ornitomímidos tenían plumas y los adultos portaban estructuras en forma de alas, como lo demuestra la presencia de perillas en el hueso del cúbito de la parte inferior del brazo, protuberancias que indican dónde se habrían adherido las plumas.

facts.statement: A diagnostic character of Gallimimus is its short hands compared to the humerus when compared to other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: Some experts suggest Gallimimus claws may have been used to dig for eggs, roots, and tubers.

facts.statement: It is more probable that Gallimimus was an omnivore, using its beak for plants and capturing small animals.
facts.quote: Parece más probable que Gallimimus fuese un omnívoro, usando su pico en las plantas y la captura de pequeños animales.

facts.statement: It has been speculated that Gallimimus may have fed on insects, small worms, and supplemented its diet with plants and eggs.
facts.quote: Sobre el Gallimimus se ha especulado sobre su dieta, sugiriendo que pudo haberse alimentado de insectos y de pequeños gusanos y pudo complementar su dieta insectívora con algunas plantas y huevos.

facts.statement: The head of Gallimimus was very small and light compared to its vertebral column.

facts.statement: Viewed from above, the beak of Gallimimus was almost spatulate, spoon-shaped, wide, and rounded at the tip.

facts.statement: The eye sockets of Gallimimus were large and oriented to the sides, similar to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Las cuencas de los ojos eran grandes y estaban orientadas hacia los lados, como en otros ornitomímidos.

facts.statement: The internal nostrils of Gallimimus were large and positioned far back on the palate.
facts.quote: Las narinas internas, aberturas internas para el pasaje nasal, eran grandes y estaban colocadas muy atrás en el paladar

facts.statement: The inner side of the beak had small, tightly packed, and uniformly spaced columnar structures.
